origin: Original workshop built by Muse (AI assistant) on 20 November 2026 at Steven Powell's direction, from the wave-2 candidate list in the Everyday Cool ideas side chat that morning: he picked Sound and Time from the list and set the order himself ('start with sound and time'), this room being the second of the pair. The room carries a sundial bench (hour lines by tan(angle) = sin(latitude) × tan(hour angle), with the equation of time and the longitude shift itemised — in Defiance, Ohio, the bench's default place, a sundial reads about 24 minutes behind the clock on 20 November, 37 of those minutes from longitude alone), a leap-year machine running any year through the Gregorian gates with the calendar's 365.2425-day average and its drift printed beside the verdict, a time-zones bench reading one entered UTC moment in seven cities at standard offsets with daylight saving confessed city by city, a scale ladder from a heartbeat to the age of the Earth with a heartbeats-in-a-lifetime bench landing near three billion, a pendulum bench animated at the period its length dictates (the seconds pendulum, 0.994 m, named when the slider reaches it), and a days-between-dates bench counting in the proleptic Gregorian calendar with the Julian switch flagged on its face. The banner shows a friendly robot holding an open brass pocket watch, studying a stone sundial with a tall triangular gnomon, an hourglass with its sand mid-fall and a plain-faced clock on the bench. It enters the catalog under 'Science,' immediately after Everyday Sound, as the twelfth door of The STEM Room. This folder is the maintained original.
